title: DKA 6 of 7, cardiac step-down: type 1 diabetes, DKA from a silent NSTEMI, potassium 3.3 on insulin, stent and radial hematoma (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by a silent NSTEMI (glucose 540, venous pH 7.21, bicarbonate 12, anion gap 24, BHB 5.8; hs-troponin I 185 to 1,420 ng/L; lateral ST depression) in type 1 diabetes; potassium 3.3 with PVCs on the insulin (held, four peripheral KCl riders), heparin, right radial PCI with a drug-eluting stent, dual antiplatelet therapy, a radial-site hematoma, nicotine withdrawal and a commercial driver license at stake
desc: Mon 11/16 0700 to Thu 11/19 0700. A 45-year-old bus driver with type 1 diabetes arrives on the cardiac step-down unit in DKA from a silent heart attack; care covers the potassium drop on insulin, heparin, a stent and a driver-license worry. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
